This guide instructs you through caching a path of your Application for the first time. By the end you will have:

- A cache setting that keeps a copy of each response for 300 seconds.
- A [Rules Engine](/en/documentation/platform/applications/rules-engine/) rule that applies the setting to one path prefix.
- The cache status of a response, read from its `x-cache` header.

The result rests on four objects, in this order. The **Application** has [Cache](/en/documentation/platform/applications/cache/) on, as every Application does. The **cache setting** belongs to the Application. It holds the time to live (TTL), how long Azion keeps a copy. It also holds what Azion does with that copy.

The **rule**, also on the Application, matches requests by path and applies the setting through the _Set Cache Policy_ behavior. A cache setting acts only once a rule applies it. A matching **request** is answered from the stored copy when one exists. With the `Pragma: azion-debug-cache` header, its response reports `HIT` in `x-cache`.

---

## Create a cache setting

A cache setting holds how long Azion keeps a copy of a response, and what Azion does with that copy. This one keeps each copy for 300 seconds.

<Tabs client:visible sharedStore="interface">

<Fragment slot="panel.console">

### Console

To create the cache setting in Azion Console:

<DocSteps>
  <DocStep title="Open the Application">

  Access [Azion Console](https://console.azion.com/) > **Applications**, then select the Application that serves your content.

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Go to the Cache Settings tab" />
  <DocStep title="Select + Cache" />
  <DocStep title="Name the cache setting">

  In **Name**, enter `static-assets`.

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Keep Override cache behavior selected">

  Under **Cache**, keep _Override cache behavior_ selected. With this option, **Max Age** replaces the TTL the origin sends.

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Set Max Age">

  In **Max Age**, replace `60` with `300`.

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Select Save" />
</DocSteps>

The new setting appears in the **Cache Settings** list, which shows its **Name**, **Browser Cache**, and **Cache**.

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.cli">

### CLI

To create the cache setting with the Azion CLI, replace `<application_id>` with the ID of your Application:

<DocSteps>
  <DocStep title="Save the request body">

  The command reads the setting from a JSON file. `stale_cache` turns on stale cache, as Azion Console does for a new setting. Save this body as `cache-setting.json`:

  <Code client:visible lang="json" code={`{
    "name": "static-assets",
    "browser_cache": { "behavior": "honor" },
    "modules": {
      "cache": {
        "behavior": "override",
        "max_age": 300,
        "stale_cache": { "enabled": true }
      }
    }
  }`} />

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Run the create command">

  <Code client:visible lang="bash" code={`azion create cache-setting --application-id <application_id> --file cache-setting.json`} />

  The command confirms the setting and returns its ID:

  ```text
  Created Cache Settings configuration with ID 123460
  ```

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Read the setting back">

  Replace `123460` with the ID the create command returned:

  <Code client:visible lang="bash" code={`azion describe cache-setting --application-id <application_id> --cache-setting-id 123460 --format json`} />

  The output reports `modules.cache.max_age` as `300`.

  </DocStep>
</DocSteps>

The cache setting exists on the Application. Record its ID: the rule in the next stage applies the setting by that ID.

:::note
Only the request body, passed with `--file`, sets `max_age`, the cache behavior, stale cache, and Large File Optimization. `--tiered-caching-enabled` fails without the `override` behavior, and only the body sets that behavior. For every flag the command accepts, refer to [Azion CLI cache-setting](/en/documentation/devtools/cli/resources/cache-setting/#create).
:::

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.api">

### API

To create the cache setting with the Azion API, replace `[TOKEN VALUE]` with your personal token. Replace `<application_id>` with the ID of your Application:

<DocSteps>
  <DocStep title="Send the create request">

  `stale_cache` turns on stale cache, as Azion Console does for a new setting:

  <Code client:visible lang="bash" code={`curl --request POST \\
    --url https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/applications/<application_id>/cache_settings \\
    --header 'Accept: application/json' \\
    --header 'Authorization: Token [TOKEN VALUE]' \\
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
    --data '{
    "name": "static-assets",
    "browser_cache": { "behavior": "honor" },
    "modules": {
      "cache": {
        "behavior": "override",
        "max_age": 300,
        "stale_cache": { "enabled": true }
      }
    }
  }'`} />

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Read the response">

  A `201` carries the setting, with its defaults filled in. This excerpt leaves out `modules.application_accelerator` and `created_at`:

  ```json
  {
    "state": "executed",
    "data": {
      "id": 123459,
      "name": "static-assets",
      "browser_cache": { "behavior": "honor", "max_age": 0 },
      "modules": {
        "cache": {
          "behavior": "override",
          "max_age": 300,
          "stale_cache": { "enabled": true },
          "large_file_cache": { "enabled": false, "offset": 1024 },
          "tiered_cache": { "enabled": false }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  ```

  </DocStep>
</DocSteps>

The cache setting exists on the Application. Record the `id`: the rule in the next stage applies the setting by that ID.

</Fragment>

</Tabs>

:::note
A Max Age below 60 seconds, in the `modules.cache.max_age` field, requires [Application Accelerator](/en/documentation/platform/applications/application-accelerator/) on the Application.
:::

---

## Apply the setting with a rule

A cache setting acts only through a rule that applies it. This rule applies `static-assets` to every request whose path matches a prefix you choose.

<Tabs client:visible sharedStore="interface">

<Fragment slot="panel.console">

### Console

To create the rule in Azion Console:

<DocSteps>
  <DocStep title="Open the Application">

  Access [Azion Console](https://console.azion.com/) > **Applications**, then select the Application that serves your content.

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Go to the Rules Engine tab" />
  <DocStep title="Select + Rule" />
  <DocStep title="Name the rule">

  In **Name**, enter `cache-static-assets`.

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Select Request Phase" />
  <DocStep title="Set the criteria">

  Under **Criteria**, select `${uri}` and _starts with_. As the argument, enter `/static/`, or the path prefix of your object.

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Add the Set Cache Policy behavior">

  Under **Behaviors**, select **Set Cache Policy**, then select `static-assets`.

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Select Save" />
</DocSteps>

The rule appears in the list and applies `static-assets` to every request whose path starts with `/static/`.

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.cli">

### CLI

To create the rule with the Azion CLI, replace `<application_id>` with the ID of your Application:

<DocSteps>
  <DocStep title="Save the request body">

  The command reads the rule from a JSON file. Save this body as `rule.json`, and replace `123460` with the ID of the cache setting from the previous stage. If your object sits under another prefix, replace `/static/` with it:

  <Code client:visible lang="json" code={`{
    "name": "cache-static-assets",
    "active": true,
    "criteria": [
      [
        {
          "conditional": "if",
          "variable": "\${uri}",
          "operator": "starts_with",
          "argument": "/static/"
        }
      ]
    ],
    "behaviors": [
      {
        "type": "set_cache_policy",
        "attributes": { "value": 123460 }
      }
    ]
  }`} />

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Run the create command">

  <Code client:visible lang="bash" code={`azion create rules-engine --application-id <application_id> --phase request --file rule.json`} />

  The command confirms the rule and returns its ID:

  ```text
  Created Rules Engine with ID 234570
  ```

  </DocStep>
</DocSteps>

The rule exists on the Application and applies `static-assets` to every request whose path starts with `/static/`.

</Fragment>

<Fragment slot="panel.api">

### API

To create the rule with the Azion API, replace `[TOKEN VALUE]` with your personal token. Replace `<application_id>` with the ID of your Application:

<DocSteps>
  <DocStep title="Save the request body">

  Save this body as `rule.json`, and replace `123459` with the ID of the cache setting from the previous stage. If your object sits under another prefix, replace `/static/` with it:

  <Code client:visible lang="json" code={`{
    "name": "cache-static-assets",
    "active": true,
    "criteria": [
      [
        {
          "conditional": "if",
          "variable": "\${uri}",
          "operator": "starts_with",
          "argument": "/static/"
        }
      ]
    ],
    "behaviors": [
      {
        "type": "set_cache_policy",
        "attributes": { "value": 123459 }
      }
    ]
  }`} />

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Send the create request">

  <Code client:visible lang="bash" code={`curl --request POST \\
    --url https://api.azion.com/v4/workspace/applications/<application_id>/request_rules \\
    --header 'Accept: application/json' \\
    --header 'Authorization: Token [TOKEN VALUE]' \\
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
    --data @rule.json`} />

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Read the response">

  A `202` carries the rule, and the state `pending` means the platform is still applying it. This excerpt leaves out `criteria`, `description`, `order`, `last_editor`, `last_modified`, and `created_at`:

  ```json
  {
    "state": "pending",
    "data": {
      "id": 234569,
      "name": "cache-static-assets",
      "active": true,
      "behaviors": [
        {
          "type": "set_cache_policy",
          "attributes": { "value": 123459 }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
  ```

  </DocStep>
</DocSteps>

The rule exists on the Application and applies `static-assets` to every request whose path starts with `/static/`.

</Fragment>

</Tabs>

:::note
A new rule can take a few minutes to propagate. Wait before you check the cache status.
:::

---

## Check the cache status

The request header `Pragma: azion-debug-cache` makes the response carry two debug headers. `x-cache` holds the cache status, the IP of the server that answered, and the protocol. `x-cache-key` holds the key that indexes the copy.

<DocSteps>
  <DocStep title="Request the object with the debug header">

  Request an object under the path the rule matches, with your own host and path:

  <Code client:visible lang="bash" code={`curl -sI -H "Pragma: azion-debug-cache" https://www.example.com/static/site.js`} />

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Read the cache status">

  The response carries the two debug headers. Under HTTP/2, the header names arrive in lowercase:

  ```text
  x-cache: MISS from 192.0.2.10 with HTTP/2.0
  x-cache-key: httpswww.example.com/static/site.js
  ```

  `MISS` means the object was not in the cache. Azion fetched it from the origin and may store the response.

  </DocStep>
  <DocStep title="Run the same command again" />
  <DocStep title="Read the cache status again">

  A response answered from the stored copy carries `HIT`. `x-cache` also names the server that answered. Each server keeps its own copy, so a request that another server answers can report `MISS` once more. Run the command again.

  </DocStep>
</DocSteps>

Your Application now keeps a copy of each matching response for 300 seconds. `x-cache` tells you when a response came from that copy. A response can also carry another status, such as `REVALIDATED`. For every status value, refer to [Cache keys](/en/documentation/platform/applications/cache/cache-keys/#cache-status).
